terminal_transcript.observations: The first live session connects to the JTAG UART and emits LCVEX25 BOOT, CAL-WAIT, DDR-FAIL, READY and startup RXDBG before any command input.

terminal_result.observations: The runner reports connected=true, boot_ok=true, ready_ok=true, input byte 0x3f, and then stops on the first missing status response; p/d/Z are not sent.

evidence_summary.observations: The recorded historical chain is candidate programmer PASS followed by BOOT/READY and terminal evidence; the candidate configuration section has no candidate post-program design-hash predicate.

script.observation: The ignored local script artifact contains an intended final design-hash check and result fields. No remote script hash is included in T-021 evidence, and the captured candidate log/result do not contain those final fields.

script_vs_execution.conclusion: T-021's actual accepted candidate run proves exact SOF identity, quartus_pgm/configuration/JTAG-ID success, and a subsequent candidate-specific BOOT/READY/live-terminal chain. It does not prove that a post-program candidate design hash was an executed acceptance prerequisite. The intended script gate and the raw execution artifacts are inconsistent; the raw execution must govern this audit.

proven: The candidate quartus_pgm transactions configured the exact frozen SOF according to tool/configuration/operation/checksum/JTAG-ID markers.
The task-owned jtagconfig path can see cable/JTAG ID but did not expose a candidate design hash.
The preserved standard server can keep reporting the old golden hash and UART/PHY after candidate programming.
Golden restore and postflight are independently proven.
not_proven: The candidate live design hash after configuration.
That the preserved standard-server golden hash is the live candidate identity.
Any candidate BOOT/READY/RX evidence in T-031; terminal was correctly skipped.

searched.finding: The documented reads are ordinary jtagconfig and owned-server jtagconfig via QUARTUS_JTAG_CLIENT_CONFIG/NO_LOCAL_SERVER. quartus_pgm -l is explicitly marked unexecuted/unverified and only concerns cable listing.
Read-only standard jtagconfig rescan can recover JTAG UART without restarting the standard server, but the evidence is golden-only and gives no candidate live-hash method.
Two delayed standard-server rescans after candidate configuration still report golden hash and UART, explicitly excluding stale-node recovery as a candidate identity proof.
T-031 exhausted owned, standard-while-owned, final standard and one delayed rescan using jtagconfig -n; none exposed the candidate hash without changing/terminating the preserved standard server.

supported_live_hash_search.conclusion: No supported, evidenced method was found for reading a candidate live design hash while preserving the standard server and avoiding reset/power. The known read-only rescan is diagnostic only; absence of evidence is not replaced by an invented method.

decision.why: A strict prior candidate-hash gate would block the next board test on an observability limitation that T-021 did not actually require and T-031 could not satisfy. The alternative is a fail-closed composite proof; it is not a waiver and does not treat the standard-server cache or programmer success as candidate identity.

program_gate.standard_server: Preserve the single identified standard jtagserver; do not stop it.
required_markers: Quartus Prime Programmer was successful. 0 errors, 0 warnings

order: Stop only the candidate task-owned programming server and preserve the standard server.
Start the first and only candidate live terminal session.
Before sending any byte, require the candidate-unique startup sequence: LCVEX25 BOOT; CAL-(OK|WAIT|FAIL); DDR-(OK|FAIL); READY; startup/autonomous RXDBG.
Require the initial RXDBG 00000000 00000000 and a later nonzero-read/zero-event RXDBG TX-drain page before the first '?'.
live_terminal_identity_gate.fail_closed: If any startup marker is absent, out of order, or the live session cannot connect, send no byte, stop only task-owned terminal/server, and perform the one golden restore. A preserved standard-server hash cannot rescue this failure.

paced_functional_gates.rule: Send one raw byte only after the preceding response; stop at the first missing response.
paced_functional_gates.rxdbg_gate: Retain startup/autonomous RXDBG and final RXDBG count/byte evidence.
paced_functional_gates.rxpath_gate: Retain bridge=PoC=dmem, final low16 0xA45A, four valid events per layer and zero fault bits.
paced_functional_gates.rxcpu_gate: Retain four valid getc/dispatch events, final getc low16 0xA45A, dispatch class=5/byte=0x5A and positive putc/TX progress.

rollback_and_retry_policy.golden_identity_after_restore: Require exact golden SOF bytes/SHA/checksum, JTAG ID, final golden design hash, JTAG UART/PHY nodes, preserved standard server, zero residual task processes and free port 1310.
rollback_and_retry_policy.note: The next task is allowed exactly one candidate program and exactly one golden restore. A failure is terminal for that task; do not hide retries in wrapper/debug scripts.

decision.preserved_standard_hash_policy: The standard server's cached golden hash and UART/PHY enumeration are diagnostic context only. They must never be recorded as the candidate live identity.

risks: The candidate-unique BOOT marker must remain part of the frozen candidate firmware contract; if a future candidate or golden emits the same marker, the contract must be re-reviewed rather than silently accepted.
T-021's ignored script artifact and raw execution disagree about post-program hash output; future tasks must hash and archive the exact remote script before execution.
T-031's three successful quartus_pgm transactions show that programmer success alone cannot establish live candidate identity or functional acceptance.
No candidate terminal evidence exists in T-031 because its identity gate failed; no RXDBG/RXPATH/RXCPU result may be backfilled from T-021.

integration_decision.artifact_hash_recheck: PASS; all accessible path/SHA256 pairs match
integration_decision.classification: fail-closed live identity observability correction, not a waiver
integration_decision.next_board_limits: exactly one candidate quartus_pgm transaction, one live terminal session and one golden restore; zero internal retries

conclusion: Use the composite live identity contract for the next board test: freeze candidate bytes/SHA/checksum/design-hash metadata; perform one exact task-owned quartus_pgm transaction with path/cable/JTAG-ID/configuration/0-error markers; then require the first live terminal to emit candidate-unique LCVEX25 BOOT, CAL, DDR, READY and startup/autonomous RXDBG before any byte. Preserve the paced ?/p/d/Z, RXDBG/RXPATH/RXCPU gates and always perform exactly one golden restore. The contract is fail-closed, does not waive the absent candidate live hash, and never treats a preserved standard-server cache or programmer PASS as live identity or functional PASS.
next: Parent review; only then dispatch a new board task with one candidate program, one golden restore, and no internal debug retries.
